name: ExprForge (inline)
comment: Phase 1b, per docs/editor-support-spec.md: this is where fn`...`/expr`...` is actually authored day-to-day -- a tagged-template injection, same pattern VS Code's own graphql/styled-components/sql extensions use. Depends on exprforge.tmLanguage.json's own patterns (source.exprforge, included below), not a duplicate grammar. `${...}` interpolation switches back to the HOST language's own grammar for its contents (a real spliced-in Node or JS value, see expr.js's own header comment on HOLE tokens) -- it is deliberately NOT exprforge grammar in there.

exprforge-template.comment: Matches `expr` or `fn` immediately followed by a backtick -- the exact same 'called as a tagged template' shape expr.js's/fn.js's own header comments describe. The tag identifier itself is captured as a function-name-ish scope so it reads as 'this is the exprforge tag', not a a variable.
exprforge-template.name: meta.embedded.block.exprforge

interpolation.comment: ${...} splices in a real host-language value (an existing AST Node, or a plain number auto-wrapped via num() -- see expr.js's holeToNode) -- switches back to the actual JS/TS grammar for its contents, not exprforge's.
interpolation.name: meta.embedded.line.js
